scores.title: Pedro Jakubowski - Ibeji IV
scores.instrumentation: Candidate Pascale Jakubowski Ibéji IV: soprano saxophone and piano.
demands: The inspected opening page combines long slurred lines, frequent accidentals and rapidly beamed descending and ascending figures.
Dynamics include ppp, p, mf and f, with repeated hairpins and abrupt changes.
Multiphonic chords appear with fingering diagrams and timed holds, including four, five and six seconds.
The opening solo’s footnote directs the saxophonist to play into the open piano while its resonance pedal remains depressed. This makes instrument placement and resonance part of preparation.
The page requests a lament-like, flexible character. Later pages, full range, duration, ensemble passages and the complete multiphonic vocabulary remain unverified.
scores.scope: One actual notation page inspected visually: first music page of the public Musik Fabrik soprano/piano sample on Sheet Music Plus. It bears copyright 1999 Éditions de la Fabrique Musique. Claims are limited to that opening solo page, not all 27 pages.

scores.title: Four Grounds
scores.instrumentation: Oboe or soprano saxophone, horn and timpani
demands: Theodore Presser identifies edition 494-01515, Tritone Press & Tenuto Publications, with soprano saxophone and oboe alternatives. Randall Faust’s catalog explicitly names horn and timpani.

Faust’s Western Illinois University program notes describe four movements: Allegro, Adagio, Allegro and Allegro molto. He describes a melodic repeating bass pattern in timpani beneath interwoven oboe and horn lines. This is the premiere participant’s account of the oboe scoring.
A soprano performance requires horn and timpani partners. No soprano notation was inspected, so transposition, written range, articulations and detailed ensemble demands remain unverified.
